subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment follow-up and upgrades
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment follow-up and next steps

Hi Carlos / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to hear more about LegacyBank's on-prem plans. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size the Private (air-gapped) proposal correctly:

- Desired deployment: fully air-gapped Private deployment (no outbound internet from compute nodes).
- Primary concerns you called out: offline upgrade process, hardware validation, maintenance windows, and auditability for SOC 2.
- Immediate ask from Redwood: hardware inventory + confirmation of bastion/update mechanism (USB, approved jump host, or temporary allowed egress).

Could you confirm:
1) The expected GPU counts and types per node (e.g., A100 40GB / A100 80GB / H100).
2) Whether there is an approved bastion or if upgrades must be purely USB-signed-image installs.
3) Maintenance window cadence and blackout dates for production.

I've looped in Rishi (our Private deployment engineer) to answer the upgrade and packaging questions. I'll attach our requirements doc and a network matrix so you can validate with your infra team.

Next steps: if you can share the inventory and let us know a good time for a technical workshop (30-60 min), Rishi and I will produce a draft SOW and target timelines.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Carlos Mendoza <carlos.mendoza@legacybank.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya@legacybank.com>, LegacyBank - Infra Team <infra@legacybank.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment follow-up and next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap. Quick answers from infra:

- Hardware: Planning for 4 nodes initially, each with 8x A100 40GB (we may expand in Q3). Each node has ~1TB NVMe for model/cache and 4TB SATA for long-term logs.
- OS: RHEL 8.x (CIS-hardened).
- Network: Compute nodes cannot reach the public internet. We have a hardened bastion host in a separate management VLAN that can be used for pulling approved artifacts after manual approvals.
- Upgrades: Must be approved by our Change Management board. Preferred method is signed offline bundles we can apply from a secure USB or pull from an internal secure artifact repo that the bastion can access (no direct internet).
- Maintenance: Monthly 2-hour windows (first Sat each month). Emergency security patches possible outside window with approval.

We need details on how Redwood signs upgrade bundles, verification steps, and whether you provide a fully offline installer image (ISO/PKG) we can import. Also curious about the minimum controller footprint and HA requirements for the control plane in air-gapped mode.

I've attached our internal inventory/notes (internal matrix). Happy to schedule the technical workshop next week.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendoza
Senior Infrastructure Manager — LegacyBank
carlos.mendoza@legacybank.com

Attachment (stub): legacybank_infra_matrix.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendoza <carlos.mendoza@legacybank.com>, Priya Shah <priya@legacybank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem / Air-gapped deployment follow-up and next steps

Hi Carlos / Priya —

Thanks for the details — that aligns with a common LegacyBank-style deployment. A few clarifications and how Redwood Private supports this: 

1) Offline installer and signed bundles:
- We provide a signed offline installer bundle (tar.gz / ISO) for air-gapped installs. Each bundle is GPG-signed; we include SHA256 checksums and a signing certificate you can verify offline.
- For upgrades we provide patch bundles (minor) and full upgrade images (major). Both are signed; you can apply via USB or place them on your internal artifact repo for the bastion to pull.

2) Upgrade verification and change control:
- Each bundle includes a manifest + pre/post-check scripts. We recommend running pre-checks inside a staging network identical to prod before applying.
- Emergency patches: we can provide expedited signed patches; those are mapped to an internal ticket and signed with an emergency key.

3) Controller footprint / HA:
- Minimum: 3 controller nodes (control plane) for HA (can be smaller for PoC). We recommend 2 GPUs for controller VMs (or small CPU-only for bootstrap) and at least 3 worker nodes in production for failover.
- For your 4x 8-GPU nodes plan, controllers can be VMs in a separate management cluster. We will provide an HA topology diagram in the workshop.

4) Hardware and storage:
- NVMe for KV cache (1TB per node is OK). We recommend an additional SSD pool for model staging (2x model copies for safe rollback).

Next steps (suggested):
- Tech workshop (60 min) this week to review manifests and network rules.
- You share the inventory + bastion access model.
- Redwood will deliver a draft SOW and an install/upgrade runbook (attached).

I'm attaching our on-prem requirements doc and the recommended network matrix for your infra team to validate. Let me know two windows that work for the workshop and we'll send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Private
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
